h1: Cold saws — manual and semi-automatic circular saws, 9″ to 16″ blades
intro: A cold saw cuts metal with a slow-turning, coolant-flooded circular blade instead of a hot abrasive disc, leaving a square, burr-free end that is cool to the touch and ready to weld. This page has the manual and semi-automatic cold saws for the fabrication shop: ISITAN's wet-type SFC 275 and 315 pull-down saws with a manual or pneumatic vise and the semi-automatic SFC 350-VX with a hydro-pneumatic head, all mitring 45° both ways; NovoTech's value-line saws, built in China — gear-driven manual CS saws with 9 – 14″ blades, the PDS-315H semi-automatic hydraulic saw and the PDS-400 heavy-duty saw with a 16″ blade; abrasive cut-off saws with 12 – 16″ wheels; and roller stands, a roller conveyor with a digital length stop and a measuring roller table. Each family below has its full specification table and photos. For production saws that feed, cut and count by themselves, see the automatic cold saws. CSA-approved panels and support from Mississauga, ON, Canada.

faq.a: The SFC V clamps with a hand vise — the simplest saw for occasional cuts. The SFC VP clamps with air at the pull of a lever, which saves time on every cut and holds short pieces better. The SFC 350-VX runs a semi-automatic cycle from a foot switch with a regulated head descent, for batches of the same part without an operator on the handle.

faq.q: Cold saw or abrasive chop saw?
faq.a: An abrasive chop saw grinds through the steel at high speed, leaving a hot, burred, slightly bevelled end and sparks. A cold saw cuts with a slow HSS blade (45–90 rpm) under coolant, so the cut is square, cool to the touch, burr-free and ready to weld or fit — and the blade is resharpened dozens of times instead of thrown away.

A standard HSS blade cuts mild steel and aluminum. For medium-hard steel we fit TiN-coated blades, TiCN for high-strength steel and TiAlN for stainless. The blade bore is 32 mm with two Ø11 mm pin holes on all SFC models, so blades are readily available in Canada.

faq.q: What voltage do these machines run on?
faq.a: Three-phase machines are supplied for 600 V as standard with a CSA-approved panel; 208 V, 240 V and 480 V 3-phase are available on request, and 240 V single-phase on models whose main motor is 2.2 kW (3 HP) or less — a machine with a motor above 2.2 kW must run on three-phase power and cannot be converted to 240 V single-phase. Manual machines have no electrics.
